query: A Flame That Stays {flag(bloomer_damped): She comes by one evening, the grey bead on its cord. "I know it's only glass," she says. "I keep it in my pocket anyway." She lights a candle with her finger, small and steady, to show you.|She comes by one evening with a candle she lit at noon and has kept burning, small and steady, all day. "Look," she says. "It stays."} Write to the castle for her {flag(bloomer_promise): You keep your promise to her father and write to the castle that night|You write to the castle that night}: what she can do, what she learned with no teacher but you, and that some people come late to things. You pay the postage; she walks it to the post office herself. Leave her your practice candle {flag(bloomer_promise): You never did ask at the castle. Instead you leave her|You leave her} the practice candle you've had since your first week, the one you learned on, burned down to a stub. A month later a letter comes with a drawing of the stub, still lit.
